claims.sourceText: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The same fact sheet: 'The aircraft made its first flight in February 1982, and by the conclusion of the program in 1985, had flown 135 times. It had a digital fly-by-wire flight control system to help stabilize the aircraft. Tacit Blue had a single flush inlet on the top of the fuselage to provide air to its two engines. The aircraft was placed on display at the museum in May 1996.'

claims.sourceText: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The specifications on the same fact sheet: 'Span: 48 ft. 2 in. Height: 10 ft. 7 in. Length: 55 ft. 10 in. Weight: 30,000 lbs. Engines: Two Garrett ATF3-6 high-bypass turbofan engines. Armament: None.' Five pilots are named on a plaque mounted in the cockpit: Mr. Richard Thomas, Col. (Sel) Don Cornell, Lt. Col. Russ Easter, Lt. Col. Ken Dyson and Maj. Dan Vanderhorst.

claims.sourceText: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', scanned in the National Security Archive Area 51 briefing book NSAEBB443, https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF , opened 2026-09-18
claims.text: The U.S. Air Force fact sheet states: 'The Tacit Blue (Whale) aircraft was built to test the advances in stealth technology. The USAF, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, and the Northrop Corp. worked together from 1978 to 1985 to demonstrate that curved surfaces on an aircraft result in a low radar return signal from ground radar.'

edges.label: DARPA a named partner in the programme, 1978 to 1985
edges.note: 'The USAF, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, and the Northrop Corp. worked together from 1978 to 1985.' This is what a documented DARPA black-programme involvement actually looks like in a primary record, and it is worth having on the board next to the Fouche file's use of the same four letters.

edges.label: Northrop Corp. the airframe contractor
edges.note: The fact sheet names 'the Northrop Corp.'; the board's existing node is northrop-grumman, the successor entity after the 1994 merger, and the edge is wired to it on that basis.

edges.label: The real black-programme aircraft of the period is 48 feet across and curved, not a 200 to 600 foot triangle
edges.note: THIS EDGE EXISTS SPECIFICALLY TO STOP A LATER SESSION DRAWING THE SUPPORTIVE VERSION OF IT. The brief that produced this build asked for the reported analysis that the TR-3B derives from or is confused with TACIT BLUE. That analysis was searched for and NOT FOUND, and the USAF's own fact sheet argues against it: curved surfaces rather than a triangle, 48 ft 2 in span, programme concluded 1985, on public display since 1996.

edges.label: USAF a named partner and the publisher of the fact sheet
edges.note: The Air Force is both a programme partner and the author of the primary record, and the fact sheet is a claim about its own programme, which is exactly the case CLAUDE.md section 2 says is a primary record rather than an interested-party inference.
